data.title: D2: Diagram Scripting Language
data.author: benzguo
data.article_summary: D2是一个声明式图表脚本语言，可将文本转换为图表。用户只需描述图表内容，D2就能自动生成图像。例如，下载CLI工具后创建input.d2文件并输入文本内容，运行命令即可生成对应的图表。D2支持实时监视模式，5-10分钟即可完成入门学习，并提供速查表供参考。项目代码托管在GitHub上，文档中也提供在线Playground供用户直接测试（部分使用import的代码片段除外）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[D2语言的优势、改进方向及与其他工具的比较]

不同观点：
• [D2的动画功能扩展]
  - Coauthor of D2提出扩展动画功能的想法，希望获得反馈。
• [D2与Graphviz的比较]
  - spopejoy质疑D2存在的必要性，认为它与Graphviz非常相似。
• [D2的语法与编程语言的结合]
  - mg探讨了如何在普通编程语言中实现类似D2的语法，认为DSL（领域特定语言）对于图表是必要的。
• [D2的布局引擎]
  - aidenn0更喜欢ELK作为默认布局引擎，认为Dagre在大多数情况下不如ELK。
• [D2的稳定性和动画功能]
  - purpleidea希望D2能提供更稳定的图表布局和动画功能，以便更好地可视化DAG的变化。
• [D2的独特功能]
  - viraptor提到D2的草图模式和工具提示功能，认为这些功能使其与其他工具区别开来。
• [D2与其他工具的竞争]
  - bargainbin认为D2虽然有很多优点，但尚未成为“杀手级”程序，PlantUML和Mermaid仍有竞争力。
  - benzguo则认为D2比Mermaid更强大，尤其是在AI辅助图表生成方面。
• [D2的企业版价格问题]
  - snowfield批评D2的企业版价格过高，限制了其在企业中的使用，同时提到LLM在图表生成中的潜力。

补充讨论：
• [D2的默认主题]
  - nwmcsween希望D2能提供更美观的默认主题，以便更容易被非技术管理层接受。
• [D2的知名度]
  - benzguo和teleforce提到D2虽然已经存在一段时间，但仍然相对不为人知，需要更多推广。

Contents
D2
is a diagram scripting language that turns text to diagrams. It stands for
Declarative Diagramming
. Declarative, as in, you describe what you want diagrammed, it
generates the image.
For example, download the CLI, create a file named
input.d2
, copy paste the following,
run this command, and you get the image below.
NETWORK
USER
API SERVER
LOGS
CELL TOWER
ONLINE PORTAL
DATA PROCESSOR
SATELLITES
TRANSMITTER
UI
STORAGE
SEND
SEND
SEND
PHONE LOGS
MAKE CALL
ACCESS
DISPLAY
PERSIST
Using the CLI watch mode
â
You can finish this tour in about 5-10 minutes, and at the end, there's a cheat sheet you
can download and refer to. If you want just the bare essentials,
Getting Started
takes
~2 mins.
info
The source code for D2 is hosted here:
https://github.com/terrastruct/d2
.
The source code for these docs are here:
https://github.com/terrastruct/d2-docs
.
info
For each D2 snippet, you can hover over it to open directly in the Playground and tinker.
There's some exceptions like snippets that use imports.

data.title: NextSilicon reveals new processor chip in challenge to Intel, AMD
data.author: simojo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[NextSilicon Maverick-2芯片的技术特点、市场前景及争议]

不同观点：
• **技术优势与创新**  
  - Servethehome认为Maverick-2的设计理念合理（链接提供详细分析）。  
  - wood_spirit提到富士通A64FX的FP64性能（3TFLOP），引发对比讨论：在超算场景下，哪种芯片性价比更高？  
  - shrubble猜测架构是否类似“脉动阵列”（如Anton超算），关注技术细节。  
  - jandrewrogers质疑芯片的核心优势不明确，呼吁明确具体工作负载的优化场景。  

• **软件生态的关键性**  
  - dajonker强调软件支持（OS、编译器、语言）比硬件更重要，以树莓派的成功为例。  
  - yyyk建议采用JIT（即时编译）技术最大化利用硬件潜力。  

• **市场与竞争格局**  
  - shusaku认为NEC等老牌向量处理器厂商可能比RISC-V初创公司更具市场优势。  
  - znpy类比Annapurna Labs（后被亚马逊收购）的成功历史，看好Maverick-2潜力。  

• **政治与伦理争议**  
  - mempko和zawaideh明确抵制以色列公司，理由是反对“种族隔离”和“恐怖袭击”，引发伦理争议焦点。  

补充讨论：  
- dlcarrier指出媒体访问限制的讽刺性（机器人可访问，人类反被拦截）。  
- gdiamos希望看到具体代码示例（如saxpy/GEMM内核）以评估性能。  
- 争议点集中在技术模糊性（jandrewrogers）和政治立场（mempko/zawaideh）。

data.title: GenAI Image Editing Showdown
data.author: rzk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[AI图像生成与编辑模型的比较和功能评估]

不同观点：
• [支持Google的领先地位]  
- dangoodmanUT认为Google在图像编辑领域的理解能力和自然编辑效果远超其他模型。  
- 例子：Google模型能更清晰地理解被编辑的图像并进行自然修改。

• [对OpenAI 4o模型的批评]  
- greatgib指出GPT-4o过于道德化，频繁拒绝合法但负面的请求，且回应模式令人不适（如过度赞美）。  
- jedbrooke提到OpenAI 4o在“章鱼袜木偶”任务中未完全满足提示要求（缺少两个木偶）。  

• [对图像编辑术语的争议]  
- indigodaddy最初批评“图像编辑”术语被误用于生成新图像，后修正为网站确实包含编辑功能，但仍认为生成模型不擅长真实编辑（如移除咖啡桌）。  
- 补充：multimodal模型（如qwen3-vl-30b-a3b）和imagegpt.com在真实编辑中表现更好。  

• [模型输出透明度的疑问]  
- addend询问是否存在能生成透明背景的AI工具，指出当前许多工具输出虚假透明背景（如灰白格子）。  

补充讨论：  
- snowfield推测模型可能通过多轮生成并仅展示最佳结果来提升表现，同时质疑4o的棕色调是否为后期处理。  
- isoprophlex对评测方法提出疑问，认为依赖多模态LLM判断多次尝试的结果可能影响准确性。  
- 争议焦点：术语混淆（生成vs编辑）、模型评测方法的透明度、道德审查与功能限制的平衡。

data.title: My favorite cult sci-fi and fantasy books you may not have heard of before
data.author: bwb
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[推荐和讨论小众或经典的科幻与奇幻文学作品]

不同观点：
• [推荐经典作品集合]
  - auntienomen推荐Fantasy Masterworks系列，认为其收录了许多高质量和有影响力的作品，尽管不完美（如缺少《War for the Oaks》和Iain M Banks的作品）。
  
• [偏好小众或老旧作品]
  - Raphell认为老旧的或小众的作品更具原始创造力，不受商业公式或电影改编的影响。
  - d4rkp4ttern推荐了《Roadside Picnic》和《XX》等小众作品。
  - freetonik推荐了《The City & the City》，认为其独特且原创。
  
• [对作品的具体批评]
  - idoubtit对Van Vogt的几部作品提出批评，认为《A voyage to Arcturus》浅薄，《The worm Ouroboros》风格独特但内容重复，《The dying Earth》虽好但非最爱。
  
• [科幻与奇幻的分类争议]
  - bondarchuk质疑为何人们总是将科幻和奇幻混为一谈。
  
• [个人推荐与请求]
  - bwb请求推荐新书，提到Peter Hamilton和Greg Egan的作品。
  - DigitalHookworm推荐了Philip Jose Farmer和Theodore Sturgeon的作品。
  - xeonax强烈推荐《The Wandering Inn》。
  - aduwah推荐了几本现代小众作品如《Memoires of an imaginary friend》和《Dogs of war》。
  
• [对具体作品的争议]
  - donkey_brains质疑《Love And Chocolate》是否是一个玩笑性质的推荐。
  - Amorymeltzer强烈推荐《The Worm Ouroboros》，认为其结构独特但值得一读。

补充讨论：
• [时间对作品影响力的影响]
  - ReptileMan提到时间的流逝使得一些黄金时代的作品变得小众，如Schekley的短篇故事和《Ticket to tranai》。

data.title: Validating your ideas on strangers (2017)
data.author: tacon
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在酒吧通过向陌生人推销创意来验证想法的方法。作者偶然发现这种免费又高效的市场调研方式后，多次成功运用。文中详细描述了两个案例：一次是遇到设计师主动征求意见，另一次是作者推销自己的"与陌生人通话"应用创意。最初版本遭到批评后，作者根据陌生人反馈立即改进方案（增加防骚扰机制），第二轮测试获得明显更好的反响。作者建议创业者可以效仿这种零成本、即时反馈的"酒吧焦点小组"方法，但要保持清醒以记住反馈内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[在酒吧中随机向陌生人征求商业反馈的可行性和道德性]

不同观点：
• **反对观点**：认为这种行为侵犯了他人的私人空间，可能引起反感甚至被驱逐出酒吧。论据包括：陌生人在酒吧是为了放松而非参与商业讨论；未经请求的干扰可能导致防御性反应而非真实反馈；这种行为可能破坏酒吧的氛围（Aurornis, politelemon, pavel_lishin, neilv）。
• **支持观点**：认为在某些特定情况下（如目标客户在场或活动与酒吧氛围契合），征求反馈是可行的。例子：有人在酒吧角落测试游戏设计，因其与酒吧娱乐性质相符（tunesmith）。
• **中立观点**：指出这种方法仅在目标客户在场时有效，否则难以获得有价值的反馈（chacham15）；建议通过自我反思或阅读相关书籍（如《The Mom Test》）来改进反馈获取方式（zkmon, vasilzhigilei）。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：是否应该在非商业环境中进行商业活动，以及如何平衡商业需求与他人权益（Lerc）。
• **幽默观点**：调侃这种行为可能被用于非商业目的（如搭讪）（yard2010）；建议集体无视以避免干扰（willguest）。
• **相关资源**：多次提到《The Mom Test》一书，认为其提供了更有效的反馈获取方法（petalmind, vasilzhigilei）。

45696438.article_content:
One of my favorite ways to truly validate an idea is at a bar... on strangers.
I "discovered" this a few years ago when I was still new to NYC, and since then have used this amazing technique half a dozen times.
It was a slow Saturday, but we had a soft launch happening, and the developer was running a tad behind. I met with the project owner at a dive bar around 50th and 3rd. We were sitting there, complaining about not having launched this site 4 days before and drinking.
About an hour in, a designer broke in to our conversation, apologizing profusely, to ask for our opinions on a couple variations on some rebranding project he was presenting on Monday.
He showed us probably close to 10 different designs, of which a few were stinkers (and he knew it), but one was amazing and another was a decent second choice.
Seeing how ballsy this guy was to interrupt a couple of people having a private, albeit very loud, conversation and ask us for our free and completely unbiased advice opened my eyes.
Even as recently as just earlier this week, I was at a bar, with a buddy, spit-balling fun projects to do during downtime, when a simple Twilio app I have wanted to do came back to me.
I've called it "Talking with Strangers," but essentially it is just a website, you sign up with your Facebook account, and put in your phone number. Cell phone, land line, pay phone, who cares. You then are able to call into the "Talking with Strangers" hotline, which will ring out to a random group of members to the site. The first one to pick up is connected with you. If you are enjoying the conversation, you hit star, if you want to be reconnected with someone new, hit pound/hash. If both people star the other, your Facebook profiles are shared to each-other.
I popped over to the table behind me, with my phone as a prop, and my best used-car-salesman enthusiasm, and started pitching.
Their reaction was
notably disturbed
! I apologized, saying I had a pitch coming up, and would really like their opinions.
Well, they were much more negative toward my idea than I thought they would be!
"It's just going to be guys acting creepy toward women. Hey baby, what are you wearing?" - The female perspective.
"Yeah, there needs to be some sort of screening process." - The previously excited boyfriend who only now realized the downside.
I took their advice to heart. Sat back down with my buddy, and we brainstormed how to overcome the issues they had.
House rules you agree to on sign up (don't be a creep, dont be an asshole, treat everyone with respect unless they have been a creep/asshole).
Minimum Facebook account age.
When you hit pound it asks why. press 1 for creep, 2 for asshole, etc; 0 or # no reason.
If you have been reported x% of calls, your Facebook and phone number are banned on the service.
Five minutes later or so, I went to a completely different table, asked this other group of strangers. I pitched the new and improved idea. A markedly better response.
This is the same technique that countless large companies do every day. Focus grouping. The only real difference is it is FREE. Oh, and you get a faster response, iterate, response.
Get out to your local bar and start pitching your ideas! Just don't get so schlammered(TM) you forget your feedback... or your product.

45696438.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在酒吧通过向陌生人推销创意来验证想法的方法。作者偶然发现这种免费又高效的市场调研方式后，多次成功运用。文中详细描述了两个案例：一次是遇到设计师主动征求意见，另一次是作者推销自己的"与陌生人通话"应用创意。最初版本遭到批评后，作者根据陌生人反馈立即改进方案（增加防骚扰机制），第二轮测试获得明显更好的反响。作者建议创业者可以效仿这种零成本、即时反馈的"酒吧焦点小组"方法，但要保持清醒以记住反馈内容。
45696438.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[在酒吧中随机向陌生人征求商业反馈的可行性和道德性]

不同观点：
• **反对观点**：认为这种行为侵犯了他人的私人空间，可能引起反感甚至被驱逐出酒吧。论据包括：陌生人在酒吧是为了放松而非参与商业讨论；未经请求的干扰可能导致防御性反应而非真实反馈；这种行为可能破坏酒吧的氛围（Aurornis, politelemon, pavel_lishin, neilv）。
• **支持观点**：认为在某些特定情况下（如目标客户在场或活动与酒吧氛围契合），征求反馈是可行的。例子：有人在酒吧角落测试游戏设计，因其与酒吧娱乐性质相符（tunesmith）。
• **中立观点**：指出这种方法仅在目标客户在场时有效，否则难以获得有价值的反馈（chacham15）；建议通过自我反思或阅读相关书籍（如《The Mom Test》）来改进反馈获取方式（zkmon, vasilzhigilei）。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：是否应该在非商业环境中进行商业活动，以及如何平衡商业需求与他人权益（Lerc）。
• **幽默观点**：调侃这种行为可能被用于非商业目的（如搭讪）（yard2010）；建议集体无视以避免干扰（willguest）。
• **相关资源**：多次提到《The Mom Test》一书，认为其提供了更有效的反馈获取方法（petalmind, vasilzhigilei）。

data.title: Nvidia DGX Spark: When benchmark numbers meet production reality
data.author: RyeCatcher
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[NVIDIA DGX Spark的性能、兼容性问题及市场定位]

不同观点：
• **性能与兼容性问题**
  - [RyeCatcher]最初认为Ollama仅使用CPU，后证实GPU利用率高达96%，并修正了FP16与BF16的误解。
  - [eadwu]指出DGX Spark在特定情况下（如卷积运算）存在内存膨胀问题，但推断问题可能与驱动或内核策略相关。
  - [stuckinhell]反驳[RyeCatcher]关于PyTorch/Transformers推理不可用的说法，表示DGX Spark在运行ollama模型时表现优异。

• **软件生态与工具支持**
  - [pertymcpert]批评文章关于ARM64+CUDA生态不成熟的说法，认为缺乏证据。
  - [enum]提供解决方案，如使用PyTorch 2.9轮子并手动编译Flash Attention。
  - [aseipp]将DGX Spark用作ARM开发系统，称赞其性能接近Zen5，并提到Fedora 42的可启动性。

• **市场定位与竞争**
  - [MaKey]质疑DGX Spark的价格合理性，认为Ryzen AI Max+ 395更具性价比。
  - [MomsAVoxell]希望DGX Spark能刺激其他厂商推出类似产品，并期待其出现在笔记本电脑中，但目前认为Apple Silicon更可行。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**
  - DGX Spark的GPU推理是否可用（[RyeCatcher]与[stuckinhell]的观点对立）。
  - ARM64+CUDA生态的成熟度（[pertymcpert]的批评与[enum]的实际解决方案）。

• **其他值得注意的讨论**
  - [jsheard]提到200GbE NIC的未充分利用问题。
  - [renaudr]建议尝试TRT-LLM运行GPT-OSS-120b。
  - [semessier]指出NVIDIA产品常以MVP形式发布，存在粗糙边缘。

data.title: Wren: A classy little scripting language
data.author: Lyngbakr
data.article_summary: Wren是一款小巧、快速、基于类的并发脚本语言，融合了Smalltalk、Lua和Erlang的特点。它具有简洁现代的语法，虚拟机实现仅4000行代码，易于理解。Wren采用单遍编译器生成紧凑字节码，性能优异；以类为核心对象模型，支持轻量级纤程实现并发；适合嵌入应用，无依赖，提供易用的C API，支持C99/C++98及以上标准。可通过浏览器试用，欢迎参与开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Wren语言的特性、适用场景及其与其他语言的比较]

不同观点：
• Wren是一种优秀的嵌入式脚本语言，适合替代Lua和JS
  - 用户bragr认为Wren是Lua的良好替代品
  - 用户jossephus01赞赏Wren兼具Lua的简洁性和JS的语法熟悉度
  - 用户apitman成功用Wren编译WASM应用，认为比Lua更简单

• Wren在某些场景下存在局限性
  - 用户pcfwik指出Wren不支持C/C++风格的严格类型系统，不适合需要精确类型控制的场景
  - 用户reactordev批评Wren的继承机制不够完善，导致代码重复
  - 用户sandbags质疑Wren与Objective-C的互操作性及调试支持

补充讨论：

  - 用户NetMageSCW质疑Wren是否仍在积极开发（最近版本是4.5年前）

45671475.article_content:
Wren is a small, fast, class-based concurrent scripting language
#
Think Smalltalk in a Lua-sized package with a dash of Erlang and wrapped up in
a familiar, modern
syntax
.
System.print("Hello, world!")
class Wren {
flyTo(city) {
System.print("Flying to %(city)")
}
}
var adjectives = Fiber.new {
["small", "clean", "fast"].each {|word| Fiber.yield(word) }
}
while (!adjectives.isDone) System.print(adjectives.call())
Wren is small.
The VM implementation is under
4,000 semicolons
.
You can skim the whole thing in an afternoon. It’s
small
, but not
dense
. It is readable and
lovingly-commented
.
Wren is fast.
A fast single-pass compiler to tight bytecode, and a
compact object representation help Wren
compete with other dynamic
languages
.
Wren is class-based.
There are lots of scripting languages out there,
but many have unusual or non-existent object models. Wren places
classes
front and center.
Wren is concurrent.
Lightweight
fibers
are core to the execution
model and let you organize your program into a flock of communicating
coroutines.
Wren is a scripting language.
Wren is intended for embedding in
applications. It has no dependencies, a small standard library,
and
an easy-to-use C API
. It compiles cleanly as C99, C++98
or anything later.
You can try it
in your browser
!
If you like the sound of this,
let’s get started
.
Excited? You’re also welcome to
get involved
!

data.title: Ken Thompson recalls Unix's rowdy, lock-picking origins
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要内容是一个软件工程资讯平台"The New Stack"的用户订阅表单，要求用户填写个人信息（姓名、公司、国家等）和工作相关信息（职位级别、角色、公司规模等），以便为其推送定制化的行业新闻和资源。表单强调不会出售用户数据，并要求用户同意服务条款和隐私政策。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[早期黑客文化和UNIX历史的回顾与讨论]

不同观点：
• [对早期黑客文化的赞美]：评论者如benzible和bonoboTP强调了早期黑客文化的积极面，如创造性合作、高度信任和对工作的热爱，认为这些特质与MBA世界观和大公司文化形成鲜明对比。
• [UNIX发展史的趣闻]：twotwotwo和oersted分享了UNIX发展中的趣事，如早期用户的多样性和Bell Labs的创新工具（如电话听写服务）。
• [Ken Thompson的贡献]：kyledrake和jeffrallen提到了Ken Thompson的著名黑客技巧和他在Go语言中的贡献。
• [文化与技术的交汇]：gbacon和noufalibrahim讨论了技术如何促进社区形成，如UNIX的设计初衷和早期工具的社区功能。

补充讨论：
• [争议点]：nunez提出了一个看似无关的问题，关于1981年一首名为“Radio UNIX USA”的朋克歌曲的起源，引发了关于UNIX文化影响的讨论。
• [其他值得注意的点]：zkmon强调了变革和领导力需要对现状的质疑和一定的“丛林本能”，而constantinum和zabzonk则分享了Ken Thompson的访谈链接和对早期黑客形象的幽默评论。

这些讨论展示了早期黑客文化和UNIX历史的多样性和深远影响，同时也反映了技术发展背后的社会和文化因素。

data.title: Show HN: MyraOS – My 32-bit operating system in C and ASM (Hack Club project)
data.author: dvirbt
data.article_summary: MyraOS是一个从头开发的x86 Unix风格操作系统，主要特性包括：保护模式（GDT/IDT）、分页虚拟内存、内存管理、用户/内核模式、进程调度、多种硬件驱动（如键盘、鼠标等）、ext2文件系统、带UI组件的图形界面以及ELF加载器（支持运行真实应用如Doom游戏）。用户可通过QEMU模拟器在macOS/Linux/Windows上运行该系统。项目作者Dvir Biton开发此系统耗时较长，鼓励用户通过邮件提供反馈。该项目在GitHub上有51颗星和2个分支，主要使用C语言开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[项目赞赏、技术细节探讨、资源合作建议、开发经验分享]

不同观点：
• **项目赞赏与鼓励**  
  - 多位用户（scuff3d、danielberdit、whitehexagon等）高度评价项目，认为其技术难度和完成度值得称赞。  
  - iezepov特别提到此类“非快速原型”项目的稀缺性，对比了当前流行的“快速编码”趋势。  

• **技术细节探讨**  
  - MisterTea和userbinator对128MB内存不足的问题提出疑问，后者建议优化效率（争议焦点：现代OS是否需要更多资源 vs 历史系统的效率参考）。  
  - Levitating询问图形栈实现细节（如DOOM的软件渲染可行性）。  
  - LarsDu88质疑VGA协议的复杂性选择。  
  - liqilin1567关注大型代码库的内存管理挑战。  

• **资源与合作建议**  
  - Imustaskforhelp提议与copy.sh/v86合作提供浏览器ISO支持，并推荐开源平台oshub.org（joexbayer）。  
  - maxpert建议制作演示视频以扩大影响力。

- 部分用户（noduerme、tomjacobs）分享了个人开发经历，强调项目对技能提升的贡献。

MyraOS
A x86 Unix-like OS made entirely from scratch.
Features
Protected mode (GDT/IDT, ISRs/IRQs)
Paging and virtual memory
Memory management
Heap and dynamic memory
User-mode (ring 3) and kernel mode (ring 0)
Processes and scheduling
Drivers (PIT, RTC, Keyboard, Mouse, Framebuffer, PATA)
ext2 filesystem
UI compositor with window widgets, labels, icons, buttons, and even a custom-made font
ELF loader, which gives you the ability to run real apps
All these features let you run real games, just like Doom, giving the preloaded Doom port in MyraOS ready to be played!
So, this isn't just a toy OS or a look-alike, it's a
real OS
that can run on
real devices
How to run it?
Download the latest release from the release tab in GitHub
Download
QEMU
- an open-source machine emulator and virtualizer
After you get the latest release, you can run this on your platform:
macOS
Normal
qemu-system-i386 -cdrom MyraOS.iso -drive file=fs.img,format=raw,if=ide,index=0 -m 1024
Fullscreen
(if you are like me and want it to look real)
qemu-system-i386 -cdrom MyraOS.iso -drive file=fs.img,format=raw,if=ide,index=0 -m 1024 -full-screen
Linux
Normal
qemu-system-i386 -cdrom MyraOS.iso -drive file=fs.img,format=raw,if=ide,index=0 -m 1024
Fullscreen
qemu-system-i386 -cdrom MyraOS.iso -drive file=fs.img,format=raw,if=ide,index=0 -m 1024 -display gtk,zoom-to-fit=on -full-screen
Windows
Here, Linux/macOS or even WSL are better; use it as a last resort:
Normal
qemu-system-i386 -cdrom MyraOS.iso -drive file=fs.img,format=raw,if=ide,index=0 -m 1024
Fullscreen
qemu-system-i386 -cdrom MyraOS.iso -drive file=fs.img,format=raw,if=ide,index=0 -m 1024 -display gtk,zoom-to-fit=on -full-screen
Feedback
I really hope you like it, as I spent a lot of time on it, and I'd really appreciate any feedback you have for me.
If you have anything, from feature requests to feedback, or even if you want to talk, email me here:
dvirm.biton@gmail.com
.

data.title: How I turned Zig into my favorite language to write network programs in
data.author: 0x1997
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了他使用Zig语言编写网络程序的经历。最初他对Zig持观望态度，直到发现Zig在重写Chromaprint算法上的优势后开始尝试。在用Zig重写AcoustID索引后，性能优于之前的C++版本，但在添加服务器接口时遇到困难。为解决异步I/O问题，他开发了Zio库，模仿Go语言的并发模型，实现了高性能的协程和异步I/O操作。Zio支持网络和文件I/O、同步原语、Go风格的通道等功能，单线程性能优于Go和Rust的Tokio框架。文章最后展示了用Zio编写HTTP服务器的示例代码。

45716109.article_content:
2025-10-26
How I turned Zig into my favorite language to write network programs in
I’ve been watching the
Zig
language for a while now, given that it was created for
writing audio software (low-level, no allocations, real time). I never paid too much attention though,
it seemed a little weird to me and I didn’t see the real need. Then I saw a post from
Andrew Kelley
(creator of the language) on Hacker News, about how he reimplemented my Chromaprint algorithm in Zig, and that got me really interested.
I’ve been planning to rewrite AcoustID’s inverted index for a long time, I had a couple of prototypes, but none of the approaches felt right.
I was going through some rough times, wanted to learn something new, so I decided to use the project as an opportunity to learn Zig.
And it was great, writing Zig is a joy. The new version was faster and more scalable than the previous C++ one.
I was happy, until I wanted to add a server interface.
In the previous C++ version, I used
Qt
, which might seem very strange for a server software, but I wanted a
nice way of doing asynchronous I/O and Qt allowed me to do that. It was callback-based, but Qt has a lot of support for
making callbacks usable. In the newer prototypes, I used Go, specifically for the ease of networking and concurrency.
With Zig, I was stuck. There are some Zig HTTP servers, so I could use those. I wanted to implement my legacy TCP server as well,
and that’s a lot harder, unless I want to spawn a lot of threads. Then I made a crazy decision, to use Zig also for implementing
a clustered layer on top of my server, using NATS as a messaging system, so I wrote a
Zig NATS client
,
and that gave me a lot of experience with Zig’s networking capabilities.
Fast forward to today, I’m happy to introduce
Zio, an asynchronous I/O and concurrency library for Zig
.
If you look at the examples, you will not really see where is the asynchronous I/O, but it’s there, in the background and that’s
the point. Writing asynchronous code with callbacks is a pain. Not only that, it requires a lot of allocations, because you need
state to survive across callbacks. Zio is an implementation of Go style concurrency, but limited to what’s possible in Zig.
Zio tasks are stackful coroutines with fixed-size stacks. When you run
stream.read()
, this will initiate the I/O operation in the background
and then suspend the current task until the I/O operation is done. When it’s done, the task will be resumed, and the result will be returned.
That gives you the illusion of synchronous code, allowing for much simpler state management.
Zio support fully asynchronous network and file I/O, has synchronization primitives (mutexes, condition variables, etc.) that work with the cooperative runtime,
has Go-style channels, OS signal watches and more. Tasks can run in single-threaded mode, or multi-threaded, in which case they can migrate from thread to thread
for lower latency and better load balancing.
And it’s FAST. I don’t want to be posting benchmarks here, maybe later when I have more complex ones, but the single-threaded mode is beating any framework I’ve tried so far.
It’s much faster than both Go and Rust’s Tokio. Context switching is virtually free, comparable to a function call. The multi-threaded mode,
while still not being as robust as Go/Tokio, has comparable performance. It’s still a bit faster than either of them, but that performance
might go down as I add more fairness features.
Because it implements the standard interfaces for reader/writer, you can actually use external libraries that are unaware they are running within Zio. Here is an example of a HTTP server:

主要讨论点：[TOON格式与JSON的比较及其在LLM中的适用性]

不同观点：
• **支持TOON格式的观点**  
  - 认为TOON通过更简洁的语法（如长度标记`[0]`）可以进一步减少语义模糊性（inopinatus）。  
  - 赞赏其创新性，认为压缩格式可能提升效率（andreygrehov、awaseem）。  

• **倾向于JSON的观点**  
  - 认为JSON已经是主流且LLM对其优化更好，新格式可能影响准确性（vessenes）。  
  - 提出通过JSON的紧凑表达（如列表或字符串拼接）也能达到类似效果（3cats-in-a-coat）。  
  - 质疑TOON的鲁棒性，尤其是基于缩进的格式（chuckadams）。  

• **其他替代方案建议**  
  - 提出类似Lisp的括号语法可能更简洁且无需特殊标记（neilv）。  
  - 建议比较其他格式如YAML、BAML、TOML或固定宽度文本（AvAn12、hedgehog）。  
  - 讨论属性名是否需引号以节省token（rs186）。  

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：TOON的实际收益 vs. JSON的主流适配性（vessenes vs. 3cats-in-a-coat）。  
- **技术细节**：LLM对压缩数据的训练与推理可行性（andreygrehov）、缩进格式的脆弱性（chuckadams）。

Token-Oriented Object Notation (TOON)
Token-Oriented Object Notation
is a compact, human-readable format designed for passing structured data to Large Language Models with significantly reduced token usage.
Tip
Wrap your JSON in
encode()
before sending it to LLMs and save ~1/2 of the token cost for structured data!
Why TOON?
AI is becoming cheaper and more accessible, but larger context windows allow for larger data inputs as well.
LLM tokens still cost money
– and standard JSON is verbose and token-expensive:
{
"users"
: [
{
"id"
:
1
,
"name"
:
"
Alice
"
,
"role"
:
"
admin
"
},
{
"id"
:
2
,
"name"
:
"
Bob
"
,
"role"
:
"
user
"
}
]
}
TOON conveys the same information with
fewer tokens
:
users[2]{id,name,role}:
1,Alice,admin
2,Bob,user
Key Features
💸
Token-efficient:
typically 30–60% fewer tokens than JSON
🤿
LLM-friendly guardrails:
explicit lengths and field lists help models validate output
🍱
Minimal syntax:
removes redundant punctuation (braces, brackets, most quotes)
📐
Indentation-based structure:
replaces braces with whitespace for better readability
🧺
Tabular arrays:
declare keys once, then stream rows without repetition

data.author: noamteyssier
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了`hist-rs`，一个高效统计文件中唯一行数量的命令行工具。它比传统方法`sort | uniq -c`快25倍，支持多种功能如筛选、排序和阈值过滤。安装简单，可通过`cargo install`完成。基准测试显示，该工具在处理100M行FASTQ文件时性能显著优于同类工具`cuniq`、`huniq`等。项目主要用Rust开发，特点是高吞吐量和丰富的命令行选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[不同工具和方法在处理大规模数据时的性能和效率]

不同观点：
• ClickHouse-local 是一种高效的数据处理工具，可以快速处理各种数据任务，性能优于传统的排序和统计工具（如sort和Rust代码）。
• awk 在处理大规模数据时表现优异，尤其是在处理重复字符串时，性能优于传统的sort | uniq -c方法。
• Rust实现的工具通过优化内存分配和使用高效的哈希表，显著提高了性能。
• sort命令默认内存使用较低，可以通过增加缓冲区大小来提高性能。
• 使用哈希表的工具在处理大量唯一值时可能需要大量内存，而传统的sort | uniq方法则更适合处理无法全部装入内存的大型数据集。
• 一些工具（如unic和mmuniq）使用特殊的数据结构（如Cuckoo Filter和Bloom Filter）来提高性能。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：不同工具的性能比较，尤其是在处理大规模数据时的内存使用和速度之间的权衡。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：如何优化字符串哈希和排序（如使用StringZilla），以及如何处理近似匹配的字符串（如使用向量数据库）。

主要讨论点：[使用Go和WASM在Web开发中的优缺点及适用场景]

不同观点：
• **支持使用Go和WASM的观点**
  - 适用于科学计算等高性能场景（Imustaskforhelp）
  - 可以作为API不可用或离线时的后备方案（zikani_03）
  - 对于引入WASM功能的教学案例很有价值（zikani_03）
  - 有趣的hack，适合个人项目使用（chamomeal）

• **对Go/WASM方案的改进建议**
  - 应该允许直接导入.go文件而不是使用指令（tkzed49）
  - 应该让开发者自己实例化WASM模块以兼容JS和Go工具链（ivanjermakov）

• **质疑Go/WASM实用性的观点**
  - WASM的性能优势可能被JS->WASM->JS的开销抵消（kypro）
  - 除非是长时间的一次性计算，否则性能提升有限（kypro）
  - 如果只用于后端，不如直接使用Go开发（lisbbb）
  - 直接使用JavaScript可能更简单（pjmlp）

• **关于安全性和架构的担忧**
  - 需要警惕在前端放置业务逻辑的风险（liampulles）
  - 要避免让客户端决定业务规则的开放API（liampulles）

补充讨论：
- 有人提到了TinyGo与标准Go的兼容性问题（Imustaskforhelp）
- 讨论中出现了关于项目大小的疑问（h33t-l4x0r）
- 多个评论者分享了类似技术的个人经验（b_e_n_t_o_n, foreigner, kypro）
- 有人预测这种模式可能会变得流行（smashah）

争议焦点：

data.article_summary: 保罗·哈德森开发了一款名为Hacktivate的教育应用，旨在通过趣味游戏方式向13岁以上青少年传授黑客技术。应用包含240个"夺旗"挑战，涵盖SQL注入、加密、数据隐写等技能，采用沙盒环境确保安全性。作者希望通过模拟电影风格的趣味任务，激发新一代对计算机科学的兴趣，同时培养真实的网络安全能力。目前该应用已登陆苹果全平台，特点是每个挑战都设计独特，避免重复枯燥。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

  - xandrius和agigao认为针对儿童的游戏不应包含应用内购买，担心会潜移默化地教会孩子消费习惯。  
  - harperlee批评游戏中明显的“购买提示”按钮，认为这是对 vulnerable people（如儿童）的剥削。

  - TimByte赞赏游戏的结构化和伦理化设计，认为它以一种有趣的方式解构了黑客技术。  
  - mbsa7提到开发者Paul Hudson的教学能力，间接支持游戏的教育价值。

  - vhantz和werdl指出游戏的目标受众（儿童）与实际的苹果设备用户不匹配，认为真正对黑客技术感兴趣的孩子可能不会使用iPhone或Mac。  
  - Zhyl询问游戏与其他黑客学习平台（如Over the Wire和Hacknet）的定位差异。

  - sikimiki和bonoboTP强调自发性学习的重要性，认为真正的黑客技能来源于好奇心和实践，而非结构化教学。

45669394.article_content:
Why I’m teaching kids to hack computers
Paul Hudson,
@twostraws
, October 22nd 2025
When I was a teen, I learned about computers by trying things, breaking things, and fixing them again – relentless curiosity and experimentation, backed up by computers being much more open to investigation, allowed me to learn and grow.
Today’s computers are a lot more polished and a lot more safe, and I get why – most folks don’t want to think about the command line, don’t care about binary, and don’t even
know
about packet sniffing.
But I’m really keen to bring back the same experiences I had for a new generation, so I decided to do something about it: I built a huge “capture the flag” game that teaches kids 13+ how to do SQL injection, how to use rainbow tables to figure out hashes, how to use steganography to hide data in images, and more.
My goal was to take just a little of the glorified theatre you usually see in movies – the look and feel of games I loved like Syndicate, Command & Conquer, and Uplink – and mix it in with real-world skills around networking, cryptography, digital forensics, and more, to create something that teaches kids core computer science skills in a fun way.
I want to talk about my goals when building the app, some of the challenges I hit, the technology that’s used, and more – I hope it’s useful!
If you want to skip the reading and just try the app yourself, click here.
What’s the problem?
There’s an abundance of “learn to hack” material already out there, but a lot of it has one or more problems:
It can be dry and academic, focusing on reading theory and answering questions.
It’s often available only to specific groups at specific times, e.g. national cybersecurity competitions.
You get challenges that are very interesting, but no guidance how to solve them.
They often use shared resources, so you can’t do things like rewrite database entries or delete files.
Some of these are inevitable – if you want a serious career in cybersecurity, you do need to sit down and study a whole lot of theory!
But together these problems can create an off-putting environment: students want to know they are dealing with real tools and technologies, but they also want a clear path, they want some guidance how to move forward, and they also want it to feel
exciting
, particularly when they are just starting out.
That’s the gap I’m trying to fill – to make something structured, with scaffolded challenges that feel cinematic but teach practical skills.
Building a safe place to break things
I decided to try building something that solved these problems. Something that:
Provides 240 “capture the flag” challenges around things like SQL injection, the Linux command line, JavaScript, hashing, encryption, and more.
Teaches students the core computing, security, and logic skills needed to solve all those challenges.
Uses safe sandboxing, so that all data, servers, and hacks are done inside the game rather than affecting real targets.
My goal is
not
to turn everyone into a seasoned pentester overnight, but just to inspire a new generation of hackers to experiment, learn, and have fun in a safe and structured way.
As you might imagine, this took a lot of work.
Part of that work was building tools to simulate real-world data in a self-contained app – packet sniffing, network routing, DNS lookups, etc, all need to be able to work without the user leaving the app and even if they are offline. (I have cached DNS results for the servers used in challenges!)
But honestly the biggest part of the work was just crafting all the challenges. If this were a platform game I could just make the core game engine then put different levels in there. In contrast, cybersecurity challenges can’t repeat because it wouldn’t be fun – every challenge has to be more or less unique.
For example, in one challenge you need to discover that one PNG file actually contains several, another challenge mixes decimal/hex/octal ASCII values to spell a message, another one hides the flag in a regex crossword, and yet another one makes you log into a virtual email inbox to find the next target of a cybercriminal gang.
The end result is live now:
it’s called Hacktivate, and it’s available on iPhone, iPad, and Mac
.
What hacking looks like inside Hacktivate
There are a whole bunch of different challenges in the game, but I want to pick out a handful of them and also talk about how they were implemented.
Basic data-handling questions – hex, binary, ASCII, base64, and similar. These teach students about data representation, and were probably the easiest to make because it’s really just about them learning to recognize what things like hex look like.
Cryptography challenges. These start out with classic codes and ciphers (Caesar, Vigenère, Morse, etc) but then move onto modern hashes and encryption with SHA1/2/3, Enigma, and AES. data.title: Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics (2014)
data.author: the-mitr
data.article_summary: 《经典力学的结构与解释》第二版是由Gerald Jay Sussman和Jack Wisdom合著的力学教材，采用知识共享许可协议发布。全书共分7章及2个附录，系统介绍了拉格朗日力学、刚体运动、哈密顿力学、相空间结构、正则变换、正则演化及微扰理论等内容，涵盖了经典力学的主要理论框架和分析方法，并包含丰富的计算实例和习题。本书强调几何观点和计算方法，旨在为读者提供对经典力学原理的深入理解和实际应用能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：《Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics》一书的阅读体验、相关资源以及古典力学的教学方法。

不同观点：
• **对书籍的赞赏与期待**  
  - [noosphr] 认为“Structure and interpretation”系列书籍极具潜力，尤其是Scheme语言作为计算基底的清晰性能够帮助理解底层逻辑。
  
• **学习方法的差异**  
  - [throwaway81523] 表示通过YouTube视频学习变分法后，拉格朗日动力学才变得清晰，暗示视觉化学习可能比纯文本更有效。

• **对理论基础的疑问**  
  - [in_a_hole] 提出疑问，希望找到解释拉格朗日方法为何有效的文本，尤其是从基本原理或牛顿力学等价性出发的证明。

• **对“古典”一词的反思**  
  - [zkmon] 认为“古典”一词具有时代局限性，建议按空间尺度（如量子、人类、宇宙尺度）重新分类科学。

补充讨论：
- **相关资源**：[michaelsbradley] 提到同一作者的《Functional Differential Geometry》，扩展了相关学习材料。
- **技术问题**：[Schiphol] 询问如何运行书中的代码，反映实践操作的困难。
- **书籍制作工具**：[mindaslab] 好奇书籍的排版软件，可能是对其美观排版的认可。

争议焦点：  
- 古典力学的教学是否应从最小作用量原理直接切入（如书中做法），还是需要更基础的理论推导（如[in_a_hole]的诉求）。  
- “古典”一词的科学分类是否合理（[zkmon]的反思）。

• **[会计方法解释]** (_sword): 反驳文章观点，解释微软采用权益法会计记录OpenAI的净亏损，并利用投资抵消应税收入。
• **[交易结构质疑]** (throwaway13337): 质疑微软是否真正持有OpenAI股权，指出原始协议是收入分成而非股权投资，认为交易条件可能不利。
• **[战略防御价值]** (HWR_14): 认为微软通过与OpenAI合作保护其核心产品(Office/Windows)免受AI竞争威胁，这种战略价值无法体现在资产负债表上。

data.title: Don't forget these tags to make HTML work like you expect
data.author: FromTheArchives
data.article_summary:
这篇文章总结了创建基础HTML文件时需要包含的四个关键元素及其作用：  

1. **`<!doctype html>`**：确保浏览器以标准模式渲染页面，避免兼容性问题。  
2. **`<html lang="en">`**：声明文档语言，帮助屏幕阅读器、搜索引擎等工具正确解析内容。  
3. **`<meta charset="utf-8">`**：设置字符编码，确保特殊字符（如é、ü）和符号（如“”、©）正确显示。  
4. **`<meta name="viewport" ...>`**：适配移动设备，防止页面缩放异常。  

作者通过示例说明了缺少这些标签可能导致的问题，并调侃了现代前端开发中常见的`<div id="root">`和脚本引用。

主要讨论点：[HTML文档的DOCTYPE声明、quirks模式与标准模式、现代网站的布局问题、HTML标记的最佳实践]

不同观点：
• **quirks模式与标准模式**  
  - aragonite指出HN和paulgraham.com未声明DOCTYPE，导致页面以quirks模式渲染，并询问如何强制切换到标准模式。  
  - dinkelberg提到DOCTYPE声明中的语法错误（如缺少空格），并讨论HTML压缩工具可能导致的非规范代码。  
  - orliesaurus建议通过用户样式表或扩展修复quirks模式下的显示问题，而不依赖站点维护者更新。

• **现代网站的布局问题**  
  - notepad0x90批评许多现代网站内容仅占屏幕20%，需放大才能阅读，质疑这是否是设计缺陷。  
  - 争议焦点：这种设计是否为响应式布局的副作用，还是CSS实现不当。

• **HTML标记的最佳实践**  
  - dugmartin强调语义化标签（如`<main>`、`<nav>`）对无障碍访问的重要性。  
  - Aransentin指出部分标签（如`<html>`、`<body>`）可省略闭合，属性引号非必须，但其他用户（如daneel_w）坚持规范化的`<head>`和元信息声明。  
  - brianzelip和chrismorgan分别对`lang`属性和viewport元标签的细节提出修正建议。  
  - wpollock呼吁在HTML5样板中包含修复CSS默认样式的内联规则。

45719140.article_content:
I was watching Alex Petros’ talk and he has a slide in there titled “Incantations that make HTML work correctly”. This got me thinking about the basic snippets of HTML I’ve learned to always include in order for my website to work as I expect in the browser — like “Hey I just made a .html file on disk and am going to open it in the browser. What should be in there?” This is what comes to mind: < html lang = "en" > < meta charset = "utf-8" > < meta name = "viewport" content = "width=device-width,initial-scale=1.0" > Why each? doctype Without , browsers may switch to quirks mode, emulating legacy, pre-standards behavior. This will change how calculations work around layout, sizing, and alignment. is what you want for consistent rendering. Or if you prefer writing markup like it’s 1998. Or even if you eschew all societal norms. It’s case-insensitive so they’ll all work. html lang < html lange = "en" > Declare the document’s language. Browsers, search engines, assistive technologies, etc. can leverage it to: Get pronunciation and voice right for screen readers Improve indexing and translation accuracy Apply locale-specific tools (e.g. spell-checking) And more… Omit it and things will look ok, but lots of basic web-adjacent tools might get things wrong. Specifying it makes everything around the HTML work better and more accurately, so I always try to remember to include it. meta utf-8 This piece of info can come back from the server as a header, e.g. return new Response ( "

Hello world

" , { status : 200 , headers : { "Content-Type" : "text/html; charset=utf-8" }, } ); But I like to set it in my HTML, especially when I’m making files on disk I open manually in the browser. < meta charset = "utf-8" > This tells the browser how to interpret text, ensuring characters like é, ü, and others display correctly. So many times I’ve opened a document without this tag and things just don’t look right — like my smart quotes . For example: copy this snippet, stick it in an HTML file, and open it on your computer: < h1 > Without meta utf-8 < dl > < dt > Smart quotes < dd > “” and ‘’ < dt > Symbols < dd > ©, ™, ®, etc. < dt > Ellipsis < dd > … < dt > Emojis < dd > 👍 < dt > Non-latin characters < dd > é, ñ, etc. Things might look a bit wonky. But stick a tag in there and you’ll find some relief. Meta viewport < meta name = "viewport" content = "width=device-width,initial-scale=1.0" > Sometimes I’ll quickly prototype a little HTML and think, “Great it’s working as I expect!” Then I go open it on mobile and everything looks tiny — “[Facepalm] you forgot the meta viewport tag!” Take a look at this screenshot, where I forgot the meta viewport tag on the left but included it on the right: That ever happen to you? No, just me? Well anyway, it’s a good ‘un to include to make HTML work the way you expect. Last But Not Least… I know what you’re thinking, I forgot the most important snippet of them all for writing HTML: < div id = "root" > < script src = "bundle.js" > Lol.

data.title: WorldGrow: Generating Infinite 3D World
data.author: cdani
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了WorldGrow，一种生成无限3D世界的创新方法。该系统采用分层框架，通过块状合成和从粗到细的优化来扩展大型环境，生成具有全局连贯布局和局部细节的3D场景。这些场景适合行走和导航评估。文章提供了项目概述、成果展示（包括大规模室内示例）、引用信息，并预告了代码即将公开。该项目由多个研究机构合作开发，目前GitHub仓库已获68星标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[无限生成虚拟空间的可行性、应用场景及技术优劣]

不同观点：
• **技术可行性**
  - [fjfaase] 质疑无限生成的内存限制和种子唯一性问题，认为有限种子可能无法实现非重复的无限世界。
  - [embedding-shape] 指出当前仅为论文阶段，缺乏代码和预训练权重，对传统PCG（程序化内容生成）的优势存疑，认为可能带来更高资源消耗和更差效果。

• **应用场景**
  - [gcr] 提出该技术可用于恐怖游戏环境（如《后室》模拟器），尽管网格显式化可能不如NeRF（神经辐射场）动态生成理想，但更实用。
  - [jackdoe] 调侃期待其在《暗黑破坏神》等游戏中的应用。
  - [keyle] 认为游戏中有趣，但其他场景意义不明，甚至可能产生“建筑废料”（Architectural slop）。

• **生成内容质量**
  - [Garlef] 和 [deterministic] 均强调核心问题不是生成世界，而是生成“有趣”的世界。
  - [splintercell] 批评部分生成结果不真实，举例存在死角和突兀的巨型窗户设计。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点：技术是否真能实现“无限”生成（如种子限制与内存问题）以及生成内容的实用性与趣味性。
- 其他讨论：[theknarf] 提及与“波函数坍缩”算法的关联性，但未深入；[tantalor] 幽默联想为《离职》（Severance）模拟器；[kittikitti] 单纯表达赞赏。

data.title: Should LLMs just treat text content as an image?
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: DeepSeek发布的新OCR论文提出“光学压缩”概念：将文本转化为图像后，模型能以更高效率处理信息。研究表明，一个图像token可准确编码10个文本token的信息量，因图像token的连续特性比离散文本token表达能力更强。这一发现暗示未来AI或可通过处理文本图像而非纯文本，显著提升长文本处理效率，甚至模拟人类通过视觉处理文字的方式。尽管现有模型未专门优化此功能，但初步测试显示该方法已具可行性，可能为AI数据处理开辟新方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：将文本转换为图像输入LLM的优势与局限性

不同观点：
• **支持图像输入的观点**：
  - 图像能提供更丰富的信息层次（如字体大小、颜色、位置等），优于纯文本标记（wongarsu）
  - 实际应用中，截图输入比直接文本附件更可靠（rebeccaskinner）
  - 人类阅读依赖整体视觉感知而非逐字符处理，图像可能更贴近这种模式（mohsen1）

• **质疑图像输入的观点**：
  - 图像只是对现有文本标记缺陷的临时修补，根本问题是标记方法粗糙（wongarsu）
  - 图像嵌入可能丢失文本标记所携带的上下文语义（ghoul2）
  - 声音输入可能比图像或数字文本更符合语言本质（mannykannot/TZubiri争议）

• **技术延伸讨论**：
  - 需要开发更好的文本标记器替代当前方案（sojuz151）
  - 多维表示（3D/4D）可能是进化方向（ToJans）
  - 跨模态图像渲染成为新研究方向（themoxon）

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点：图像是否真正优于文本，或仅暴露了文本处理的不足
- 典型案例：DeepVariant基因组图像分析（bonsai_spool）与FastText/Word2Vec类比（vindex10）
- 效率问题：图像与文本的token转化率差异（aitchnyu）

45652952.article_content:
Several days ago, DeepSeek released a new
OCR paper
. OCR, or “optical character recognition”, is the process of converting an image of text - say, a scanned page of a book - into actual text content. Better OCR is obviously relevant to AI because it unlocks more text data to train language models on
1
. But there’s a more subtle reason why really good OCR might have deep implications for AI models.
Optical compression
According to the DeepSeek paper, you can pull out 10 text tokens from a single image token with near-100% accuracy. In other words, a model’s internal representation of an image is ten times as efficient as its internal representation of text. Does this mean that models shouldn’t consume text at all? When I paste a few paragraphs into ChatGPT, would it be more efficient to convert that into an image of text before sending it to the model?
Can we supply 10x or 20x more data to a model at inference time by supplying it as an image of text instead of text itself?
This is called “optical compression”. It reminds me of a
funny idea
from June of this year to save money on OpenAI transcriptions: before uploading the audio, run it through ffmpeg to speed it up by 2x. The model is smart enough to still pull out the text, and with one simple trick you’ve cut your inference costs and time by half. Optical compression is the same kind of idea: before uploading a big block of text, take a screenshot of it (and optionally downscale the quality) and upload the screenshot instead.
Some people are already sort-of doing this with existing multimodal LLMs. There’s a company
selling this as a service
, an
open-source
project, and even a
benchmark
. It seems to work okay! Bear in mind that this is not an intended use case for existing models, so it’s plausible that it could get a lot better if AI labs start actually focusing on it.
The DeepSeek paper suggests an interesting way
2
to use tighter optical compression for long-form text contexts. As the context grows, you could decrease the resolution of the oldest images so they’re cheaper to store, but are also literally blurrier. The paper suggests an analogy between this and human memory, where fresh memories are quite vivid but older ones are vaguer and have less detail.
Why would this work?
Optical compression is pretty unintuitive to many software engineers.
Why on earth would an image of text be expressible in fewer tokens than the text itself?
In terms of raw information density, an image obviously contains more information than its equivalent text. You can test this for yourself by creating a text file, screenshotting the page, and comparing the size of the image with the size of the text file: the image is about 200x larger. Intuitively, the word “dog” only contains a single word’s worth of information, while an image of the word “dog” contains information about the font, the background and text color, kerning, margins, and so on. How, then, could it be possible that a single image token can contain ten tokens worth of text?
The first explanation is that
text tokens are discrete while image tokens are continuous
. Each model has a finite number of text tokens - say, around 50,000. Each of those tokens corresponds to an embedding of, say, 1000 floating-point numbers. Text tokens thus only occupy a scattering of single points in the space of all possible embeddings. By contrast, the embedding of an image token can be sequence of those 1000 numbers. So an image token can be far more expressive than a series of text tokens.
Another way of looking at the same intuition is that
text tokens are a really inefficient way of expressing information
. This is often obscured by the fact that text tokens are a reasonably efficient way of
sharing
information, so long as the sender and receiver both know the list of all possible tokens. When you send a LLM a stream of tokens and it outputs the next one, you’re not passing around slices of a thousand numbers for each token - you’re passing a single integer that represents the token ID. But
inside the model
this is expanded into a much more inefficient representation (inefficient because it encodes some amount of information about the meaning and use of the token)
3
. So it’s not that surprising that you could do better than text tokens.
Zooming out a bit, it’s plausible to me that
processing text as images is closer to how the human brain works
. To state the obvious, humans don’t consume text as textual content; we consume it as image content (or sometimes as audio). Maybe treating text as a sub-category of image content could unlock ways of processing text that are unavailable when you’re just consuming text content. As a toy example, emoji like :) are easily-understandable as image content but require you to “already know the trick” as text content
4
.
Final thoughts
Of course, AI research is full of ideas that sounds promising but just don’t work that well. It sounds like you should be able to do this trick on current

data.article_summary: GeoUtil.com是一个在线地理工具包，提供多种免费、浏览器端运行的地理数据处理功能。主要特点包括：完全本地处理确保隐私、无需注册、支持多种地理数据格式（如GeoJSON、Shapefile、KML等）。核心工具分为四类：测量工具（距离、面积、方位角计算）、格式转换器（支持GeoJSON与其他格式互转）、坐标工具（CRS转换、坐标格式转换）、文件操作工具（合并与拆分地理数据文件）。所有工具均面向专业人士设计，适用于GIS开发、地理数据分析等场景，强调数据处理的高效性和准确性。

data.title: Rust cross-platform GPUI components
data.author: xvilka
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了GPUI Component，一个基于Rust语言的跨平台桌面应用程序UI组件库，具有60多种丰富的组件。其主要特点包括：现代化UI设计（融合macOS和Windows风格）、无状态组件、多主题支持、灵活布局、高性能虚拟化表格/列表、原生Markdown/HTML渲染、内置图表及代码编辑器（支持LSP）。文章展示了该库在Longbridge Pro应用中的实际应用，并提供了基础使用示例。此外还提及了WebView实验性功能、图标系统以及与其他框架（如Iced、egui、QT）的功能对比。该项目采用Apache 2.0许可证，目前处于开发阶段，文档尚不完善但提供多个示例参考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust UI库GPUI及其组件的完整性、可用性和未来发展前景。

不同观点：
• 对GPUI的积极评价：
  - 认为它是目前最完整的Rust UI库之一，具有丰富的组件和小部件。
  - 特别提到其展示应用令人印象深刻，展示了所有组件功能。
  - 对其未来发展持乐观态度，认为它在Rust UI生态中迈出了重要一步。

• 对GPUI的批评和担忧：
  - 指出其依赖过多（如GTK、GDK等），并且依赖其他工具包的设计令人不解。
  - 对其可访问性（如屏幕阅读器支持）表示怀疑，认为这可能是一个严重的限制因素。
  - 质疑其是否真正“原生”，尤其是在文本输入和滚动等基础功能上。

• 与其他工具的比较：
  - 提到Tauri作为Rust桌面应用开发的替代方案。
  - 比较了Qt的优势，如可视化编辑器、灵活的许可证选项和较小的二进制大小。
  - 讨论了其他Rust UI库（如iced、dioxus、fyrox-ui）的优缺点。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：
  - GPUI的依赖问题：是否合理还是设计缺陷？
  - 可访问性支持：是否足够成熟以满足无障碍需求？
  - “原生”定义：是否真正实现了原生功能？

• 其他值得注意的点：
  - 开源贡献：讨论了一些公司（如交易/加密货币公司）在开源项目中的角色。
  - 虚拟化列表和表格：被认为是UI框架中的重要功能，但许多框架缺乏。
  - 电池寿命和游戏内渲染：一些用户对GPUI在这些特定场景下的表现感兴趣。

45719004.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了GPUI Component，一个基于Rust语言的跨平台桌面应用程序UI组件库，具有60多种丰富的组件。其主要特点包括：现代化UI设计（融合macOS和Windows风格）、无状态组件、多主题支持、灵活布局、高性能虚拟化表格/列表、原生Markdown/HTML渲染、内置图表及代码编辑器（支持LSP）。文章展示了该库在Longbridge Pro应用中的实际应用，并提供了基础使用示例。此外还提及了WebView实验性功能、图标系统以及与其他框架（如Iced、egui、QT）的功能对比。该项目采用Apache 2.0许可证，目前处于开发阶段，文档尚不完善但提供多个示例参考。

不同观点：

  - 认为它是目前最完整的Rust UI库之一，具有丰富的组件和小部件。

data.title: What happened to running what you wanted on your own machine?
data.author: marbartolome
data.article_summary: 文章回顾了个人电脑从40年前的自由开放到如今逐渐封闭的演变过程。过去用户可以自由运行任何软件，而现在谷歌和苹果等科技巨头通过应用商店审核、限制侧载等方式加强对设备的控制，美其名曰保障安全，实则削弱用户自主权。作者指出这种"围墙花园"模式最早源于游戏主机厂商的利益驱动，并批评科技公司以安全为名行垄断之实，导致用户失去对设备的完全掌控权。文章警告这种趋势正在智能手机领域加速蔓延，而大多数人尚未意识到自由正在悄然消逝。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[通用计算自由度的下降趋势及其原因]

不同观点：
• **everdrive** 和 **fsf4alltemp** 认为通用计算自由度正在被侵蚀，原因包括移动设备的普及、TPM技术、市场力量和政治因素。他们担心未来法律和厂商可能进一步限制用户自由。
• **NoSalt** 和 **Gigachad** 认为当前桌面计算机仍保持高度自由，移动设备的安全限制是合理的，且用户对敏感数据保护的需求推动了这些变化。
• **trentnix** 和 **buyucu** 指出商业模式的变化是主要原因，上市公司为追求利润最大化而限制用户选择，导致市场垄断和用户权益受损。
• **lapcat** 和 **rawgabbit** 从历史角度分析，指出技术发展的路径依赖和个别决策（如微软的安全放松）对现状的影响。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：是否应该为了安全牺牲用户自由度（如 **fsf4alltemp** vs **Gigachad**）。
• **解决方案**：多人建议使用Linux（如 **mrbluecoat**、**fghorow**），但也有人指出其局限性（如 **fsf4alltemp** 提到银行服务依赖特定设备）。

45718665.article_content:
When the microcomputer first landed in homes some forty years ago, it came with a simple freedom—you could run whatever software you could get your hands on. Floppy disk from a friend? Pop it in. Shareware demo downloaded from a BBS? Go ahead! Dodgy code you wrote yourself at 2 AM? Absolutely. The computer you bought was yours. It would run whatever you told it to run, and ask no questions.
Today, that freedom is dying. What’s worse, is it’s happening so gradually that most people haven’t noticed we’re already halfway into the coffin.
News? Pegged.
There are always security risks when running code from untrusted sources. The stakes are higher these days when our computers are the gateways to our personal and financial lives.
The latest broadside fired in the war against platform freedom has been fired.  Google recently announced
new upcoming restrictions on APK installations
. Starting in 2026, Google will tightening the screws on sideloading, making it increasingly difficult to install applications that haven’t been blessed by the Play Store’s approval process. It’s being sold as a security measure, but it will make it far more difficult for users to run apps outside the official ecosystem. There is a security argument to be made, of course, because suspect code can cause all kinds of havoc on a device loaded with a user’s personal data. At the same time, security concerns have a funny way of aligning perfectly with ulterior corporate motives.
It’s a change in tack for Google, which has always had the more permissive approach to its smartphone platform. Contrast it to Apple, which has sold the iPhone as a fully locked-down device since day one. The former company said that if you own your phone, you could do what you want with it. Now, it seems Google is changing its mind ever so slightly about that. There will still be workarounds, like signing up as an Android developer and giving all your personal ID to Google, but it’s a loss to freedom whichever way you look at it.
Beginnings
Sony put a great deal of engineering into the PlayStation to ensure it would only read Sony-approved discs. Modchips sprung up as a way to get around that problem, albeit primarily so owners could play cheaper pirated games. Credit:
Libreleah
, CC BY-SA 4.0,
The walled garden concept didn’t start with smartphones. Indeed, v
ideo game consoles were a bit of a trailblazer in this space, with manufacturers taking this approach decades ago. The moment gaming became genuinely profitable, console manufacturers realized they could control their entire ecosystem. Proprietary formats, region systems, and lockout chips were all valid ways to ensure companies could levy hefty licensing fees from developers. They locked down their hardware tighter than a bank vault, and they did it for one simple reason—money. As long as the manufacturer could ensure the console wouldn’t run unapproved games, developers would have to give them a kickback for every unit sold.
By and large, the market accepted this. Consoles were single-purpose entertainment machines. Nobody expected to run their own software on a Nintendo, after all. The deal was simple—you bought a console from whichever company, and it would only play whatever they said was okay. The vast majority of consumers didn’t care about the specifics. As long as the console in question had a decent library, few would complain.
Nintendo created the 10NES copy protection system to ensure its systems would only play games approved by the company itself, in an attempt to exert quality control after the 1983 North American video game crash. Credit: Evan-Amos, public domain
There was always an underground—adapters to work around region locks, and bootleg games that relied on various hacks—with varying popularity over the years. Often, it was high prices that drove this innovation—think of the many PlayStation mod chips sold to play games off burnt CDs to avoid paying retail.
At the time, this approach largely stayed within the console gaming world. It didn’t spread to actual computers because computers were tools. You didn’t buy a PC to consume content someone else curated for you. You bought it to do whatever you wanted—write a novel, make a spreadsheet, play games, create music, or waste time on weird hobby projects. The openness wasn’t a bug, or even something anybody really thought about. It was just how computers
were.
It wasn’t just a PC thing, either—every computer on the market let you run what you wanted! It wasn’t just desktops and laptops, either; the nascent tablets and PDAs of the 1990s operated in just the same way.
Then came the iPhone, and with it, the App Store. Apple took the locked-down model and applied it to a computer you carry in your pocket. The promise was that you’d only get apps that were approved by Apple, with the implicit guarantee of a certain level of quality and functionality.
Apple is credited with pioneering the modern smartphone, and in turn, the walled garden that is t

data.title: Corrosion
data.author: cgb_
data.article_summary:
Fly.io平台遭遇了一次严重故障，原因是其分布式状态同步系统Corrosion在传播新配置时触发了Rust并发编程中的锁死问题。这次事故促使团队反思分布式系统设计的核心挑战。

文章介绍了Fly.io独特的分布式架构：采用去中心化的"竞标模式"，让每台服务器自主管理负载，而非依赖中心数据库。但为了实现全球路由，他们最初使用了HashiCorp Consul和SQLite缓存，后发现这类共识协议在跨地域场景中存在性能瓶颈。

最终团队开发了Corrosion系统，借鉴OSPF链路状态路由协议的思想，基于SWIM协议实现高效的状态同步，并将该系统开源。核心经验是：真正的分布式系统必须经历失败才能成熟。

主要讨论点：[Corrosion系统的设计、实现及其在实际生产中的挑战和解决方案]

不同观点：

  - ricardobeat赞赏文章的写作风格和技术深度。
  - conradev对cr-sqlite在生产中的应用表示赞赏。
  - cadamsdotcom对Corrosion和Consul的双系统运行模式表示认可。

  - mosura认为文章内容不够深入，建议参考蚁群优化算法。

  - soamv对cr-sqlite中nullable列的回填行为提出疑问。
  - jimmyl02对gossip协议的扩展性表示好奇，并希望了解大型系统的实际运作方式。

Image by
Annie Ruygt
Fly.io transmogrifies Docker containers into Fly Machines: micro-VMs running on our own hardware all over the world. The hardest part of running this platform isnât managing the servers, and it isnât operating the network; itâs gluing those two things together.
Several times a second, as customer CI/CD pipelines tear up or bring down
Fly Machines
, our state synchronization system blasts updates across our internal mesh, so that edge proxies from Tokyo to Amsterdam can keep the accurate routing table that allows them to route requests for applications to the nearest customer instances.
On September 1, 2024, at 3:30PM EST, a new Fly Machine came up with a new “virtual service” configuration option a developer had just shipped. Within a few seconds every proxy in our fleet had locked up hard. It was the worst outage we’ve experienced: a period during which no end-user requests could reach our customer apps at all.
Distributed systems are blast amplifiers. By propagating data across a network, they also propagate bugs in the systems that depend on that data. In the case of Corrosion, our state distribution system, those bugs propagate
quickly
. The proxy code that handled that Corrosion update had succumbed to a
notorious Rust concurrency footgun
: an
if let
expression over an
RWLock
assumed (reasonably, but incorrectly) in its
else
branch that the lock had been released. Instant and virulently contagious deadlock.
A lesson we’ve learned the hard way: never trust a distributed system without an interesting failure story. If a distributed system hasn’t ruined a weekend or kept you up overnight, you don’t understand it yet. Which is why that’s how we’re introducing Corrosion, an unconventional service discovery system we built for our platform
and  open sourced
.
Our Face-Seeking Rake
State synchronization is the hardest problem in running a platform like ours. So why build a risky new distributed system for it? Because no matter what we try, that rake is waiting for our foot. The reason is our orchestration model.
Virtually every mainstream orchestration system (including Kubernetes) relies on a centralized database to make decisions about where to place new workloads. Individual servers keep track of what they’re running, but that central database is the source of truth. At Fly.io, in order to scale across dozens of regions globally,
we flip that notion on its head
: individual servers are the source of truth for their workloads.
In our platform, our central API bids out work to what is in effect a global market of competing “worker” physical servers. By moving the authoritative source of information from a central scheduler to individual servers, we scale out without bottlenecking on a database that demands both responsiveness and consistency between SÃ£o Paulo, Virginia, and Sydney.
The bidding model is elegant, but it’s insufficient to route network requests. To allow an HTTP request in Tokyo to find the nearest instance in Sydney, we really do need some kind of global map of every app we host.
For longer than we should have, we relied on
HashiCorp Consul
to route traffic. Consul is fantastic software. Don’t build a global routing system on it. Then we
built SQLite caches of Consul
. SQLite: also fantastic. But don’t do this either.
Like an unattended turkey deep frying on the patio, truly global distributed consensus promises deliciousness while yielding only immolation.
Consensus protocols like Raft
break down over long distances. And they work against the architecture of our platform: our Consul cluster, running on the biggest iron we could buy, wasted time guaranteeing consensus for updates that couldn’t conflict in the first place.
Corrosion
To build a global routing database, we moved away from distributed consensus and took cues from actual routing protocols.
A protocol like OSPF
has the same operating model and many of the same constraints we do. OSPF is a “
link-state routing protocol
”, which, conveniently for us, means that routers are sources of truth for their own links and responsible for quickly communicating  changes to every other router, so the network can make forwarding decisions.
We have things easier than OSPF does. Its flooding algorithm can’t assume connectivity between arbitrary routers (solving that problem is the point of OSPF). But we run a global, fully connected WireGuard mesh between our servers. All we need to do is gossip efficiently.
Corrosion is a Rust program
that propagates a SQLite database with a gossip protocol.
Like Consul, our gossip protocol is
built on SWIM
. Start with the simplest, dumbest group membership protocol you can imagine: every node spams every node it learns about with heartbeats. Now, just two tweaks: first, each step of the protocol, spam a random subset of nodes, not the whole set. Then, instead of freaking out when a heartbeat fails, mark it

The last European train that travels by sea
2 days ago
Share
Save
Lottie Limb
Share
Save
Alamy
Italy's sleeper from Milan to Sicily ends with a rare rail-ferry crossing that's threatened by a new mega bridge.
Our ferry cuts through the roiling waters of the Strait of Messina under clouds that blanket all but the hems of Sicily's distant mountains. The sea passage to the Italian island doesn't want for drama. It's governed by tidal currents so strong they inspired Scylla and Charybdis, the sea monsters in Homer's Odyssey, and is overseen by a golden statue of the Madonna at the end of Messina Harbour, arm raised in blessing. But my eye is drawn to a stranger sight: the train carriages travelling across the sea on the ferry itself.
This is unique cargo. The narrow strait is the only place in Europe where passenger trains still travel by sea. Every morning, passengers aboard the
Intercity Notte
follow the same ritual: watching the train split in the southern Italian city of Villa San Giovanni, get shunted onto the ferry’s tracks and carried across to the city of Messina before being reassembled for the final run to Palermo or Syracuse.
"It is a small engineering choreography that keeps two shores and two worlds together every day: students, workers, families returning home, strait commuters, tourists who choose the slow pace of the night train," Francesca Serra, director of Intercity operations at national operator Trenitalia, tells me.
But this choreography connecting land and sea may soon come to an end.
In August, the Italian government revived long-standing plans to build a vast €13.5bn (£11.7bn)
suspension bridge
over the strait – one of the world's most ambitious engineering projects. Supporters see it as progress, while critics warn it could drain resources from southern Italy's more urgent infrastructure needs. Whether or not it's ever built, the proposal has cast a shadow over one of Europe's most poetic journeys and the sense of ritual and connection it represents.
Getty Images
Plans for a megabridge between Calabria and Sicily could mark the end of the historic train-ferry crossing (Credit: Getty Images)
When I travelled on the Intercity Notte in February 2025, none of this seemed particularly urgent. The bridge plan was still languishing in political limbo and the sea crossing felt like an evocative journey that would surely always exist. This was the backbone of an overland trip my partner and I were taking from Nottingham to Sicily, and we wound our way down through France and Turin before arriving at the grand Milano Centrale. From here, the overnight journey to Syracuse in Sicily – Italy's longest sleeper service – promised something special: a 1,489km passage through the length of Italy, linking mainland and island.
It is a small engineering choreography that keeps two shores and two worlds together every day – Francesca Serra
Our train left at 19:40 and night was closing in as we rattled down the coast, passing bright constellations of Cinque Terre towns. Compartment doors left open offered glimpses of life along the aisle: families playing cards, an old man with a cup of wine, a couple and their handsome Italian greyhound. I drifted asleep, stirred occasionally by melodic Tannoy announcements from dark platforms washed in orange light.
Around 07:00, I was woken by a knock at the door and, scrambling for my glasses, found the carriage attendant waiting patiently with a shot of espresso. A breakfast tray of juice, croissant, dry biscuits and apricot spread followed. Calabrian towns began their days beneath pale skies, which took on a moodier complexion over the Tyrrhenian Sea, flecked with lightning. We came into the salt-licked station of Villa San Giovanni just in time to see Intercity day train returning from Sicily snake out of the ferry's open bow, pulled by a sturdy locomotive.
Our train continued a little way along the track before we switched direction and were pushed into the empty vessel. I felt a jolt as our row of carriages was decoupled from the one in front and my sea views were briefly replaced by metal walls. As we were pushed into the bowels of the ferry, a well-rehearsed crew in high-vis jackets shouted instructions at each other above the burr of machinery.
Lottie Limb
The Intercity Notte is the last passenger train in Europe still ferried over a strait (Credit: Lottie Limb)
Train-ferries emerged in the late 19th Century as an enterprising answer to the question of what happens when an expanding rail network meets a large body of water. The Strait of Messina service began in 1899 and was once one of several places in Europe where passenger trains were loaded onto ferries, including between Dover and Dunkirk. After the 2019 closure of the Puttgarden-Rødby service between
Germany and Denmark
and the seasonal
Sassnitz-Trelleborg
route linking Germany and Sweden in 2020, the Intercity is now the last one running. All the rest were replaced by bridges or tunnels, or proved too ex

data.title: SETL Programming Language
data.author: usgroup
data.article_summary: SETL是一种基于数学集合理论的超高级编程语言，由纽约大学的Jacob T. Schwartz等人于1969年设计。它支持多种编程范式，提供集合和元组两种基本数据结构，支持动态类型和丰富的集合操作。SETL曾在多个平台上实现，并被用于早期Ada语言的开发。其衍生版本包括SETL2、ISETL和GNU SETL等。Python的前身ABC语言也受到了SETL的影响。SETL以其简洁的数学表达方式著称，适合处理离散数学问题。

[

[

It was originally developed at the

in the late 1960s, by a group including (Jack)
Jacob T. Schwartz
,
[
1

[
3

R.B.K. Dewar, and E. Schonberg.
[
1
]
Schwartz is credited with designing the language.
[
4
]
Design
[
edit
]
SETL provides two basic aggregate data types: (unordered)
sets
, and
tuples
.
[
1
]
[
2
]
[
5
]
The elements of sets and tuples can be of any arbitrary type, including sets and tuples themselves, except the undefined value
om
[
1
]
(sometimes capitalized:
OM
).
[
6
]
Maps
are provided as sets of
pairs
(i.e., tuples of length 2) and can have arbitrary domain and range types.
[
1
]
[
5
]
Primitive operations in SETL include set membership, union, intersection, and power set construction, among others.
[
1
]
[
6
]
SETL provides quantified boolean expressions constructed using the
universal
and
existential quantifiers
of
first-order predicate logic
.
[
1
]
[
6
]
SETL provides several
iterators
to produce a variety of loops over aggregate data structures.
[
1
]
[
7
]
Examples
[
edit
]
Print all prime numbers from 2 to
N
:
print([n in [2..N] | forall m in {2..n - 1} | n mod m > 0]);
The notation is similar to
list comprehension
.
A factorial procedure definition:
procedure factorial(n); -- calculates the factorial n!
return if n = 1 then 1 else n * factorial(n - 1) end if;
end factorial;
A more conventional SETL expression for factorial (n > 0):
*/[1..n]

[

]
Implementations of SETL were available on the
CDC 6600
,
CDC Cyber
, DEC
VAX
,
IBM/370
,
Sun
workstation and
Apollo
.
[
8
]
In the 1970s, SETL was ported to the
BESM-6
,
ES EVM
and other Russian computer systems.
[
9
]
SETL was used for an early implementation of the programming language
Ada
, named the NYU Ada/ED translator.
[
10
]
This later became the first validated Ada implementation, certified on April 11, 1983.
[
11
]
According to
Guido van Rossum
, "
Python
's predecessor,
ABC
, was inspired by SETL –
Lambert Meertens
spent a year with the SETL group at NYU before coming up with the final ABC design!"
[
12
]
Language variants
[
edit
]
SET Language 2
(SETL2), a backward incompatible descendant of SETL, was created by Kirk Snyder of the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences at
New York University
in the late 1980s.
[
13
]
Like its predecessor, it is based on the theory and notation of finite sets, but has also been influenced in
syntax
and style by the Ada language.
[
13
]
Interactive SET Language
(ISETL) is a variant of SETL used in
discrete mathematics
.
[
14
]
GNU SETL
is a command-line utility that implements and extends SETL.

data.title: AI, Wikipedia, and uncorrected machine translations of vulnerable languages
data.author: kawera
data.article_summary: 26岁的德国人Kenneth Wehr接管格陵兰语维基百科后，发现该版本存在严重问题：绝大多数文章是由不懂格陵兰语的用户通过机器翻译生成的，内容错误百出。这种现象不仅存在于格陵兰语版本，在非洲四种语言及加拿大因纽特语版本中也普遍存在，40%-60%的文章是未经修正的机翻内容。这形成了恶性循环：AI系统从这些错误数据中学习，导致翻译质量更差，而劣质翻译又被继续上传至维基百科。由于小语种网络语料稀缺，维基百科常成为AI训练的主要数据源，错误内容会进一步污染AI模型。专家指出，这种"垃圾进、垃圾出"的问题对小语种保护构成严峻挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[AI翻译和小语种维基百科的质量问题，以及语言保护的争议]

不同观点：
• **支持人工编辑与小语种保护**  
  - [simonw]提到Scots Wikipedia的案例，指出非母语者大量编辑会导致质量问题，但并非恶意  
  - [ratg13]强调格陵兰东西部语言差异大，非母语者（即使是教师）无法有效判断内容质量  

• **反对低质量AI翻译填充**  
  - [aucisson_masque]认为若无足够母语志愿者贡献，应关闭小语种维基百科而非依赖错误翻译  
  - [r2vcap]以韩语维基为例，指出社区排外导致内容质量低下，影响LLM训练数据可靠性  

• **语言自然消亡的合理性**  
  - [foxglacier]主张语言淘汰是自然现象，无需强行维持  
  - [bradley13]从历史视角提出语言更替是常态，人工干预可能无意义

45706518.article_content:
When Kenneth Wehr started managing the Greenlandic-language version of Wikipedia four years ago, his first act was to delete almost everything. It had to go, he thought, if it had any chance of surviving.
Wehr, who’s 26, isn’t from Greenland—he grew up in Germany—but he had become obsessed with the island, an autonomous Danish territory, after visiting as a teenager. He’d spent years writing obscure Wikipedia articles in his native tongue on virtually everything to do with it. He even ended up moving to Copenhagen to study Greenlandic, a language spoken by some 57,000 mostly Indigenous Inuit people scattered across dozens of far-flung Arctic villages.
The Greenlandic-language edition was added to Wikipedia around 2003, just a few years after the site launched in English. By the time Wehr took its helm nearly 20 years later, hundreds of Wikipedians had contributed to it and had collectively written some 1,500 articles totaling over tens of thousands of words. It seemed to be an impressive vindication of the crowdsourcing approach that has made Wikipedia the go-to source for information online, demonstrating that it could work even in the unlikeliest places.
There was only one problem: The Greenlandic Wikipedia was a mirage.
Related Story
Meta’s new AI model can translate speech from more than 100 languages
Read next
Virtually every single article had been published by people who did not actually speak the language. Wehr, who now teaches Greenlandic in Denmark, speculates that perhaps only one or two Greenlanders had ever contributed. But what worried him most was something else: Over time, he had noticed that a growing number of articles appeared to be copy-pasted into Wikipedia by people using machine translators. They were riddled with elementary mistakes—from grammatical blunders to meaningless words to more significant inaccuracies, like an entry that claimed Canada had only 41 inhabitants. Other pages sometimes contained random strings of letters spat out by machines that were unable to find suitable Greenlandic words to express themselves.
“It might have looked Greenlandic to [the authors], but they had no way of knowing,” complains Wehr.
“Sentences wouldn’t make sense at all, or they would have obvious errors,” he adds. “AI translators are really bad at Greenlandic.”
What Wehr describes is not unique to the Greenlandic edition.
Wikipedia is the most ambitious multilingual project after the Bible: There are editions in over 340 languages, and a further 400 even more obscure ones are being developed and tested. Many of these smaller editions have been swamped with automatically translated content as AI has become increasingly accessible. Volunteers working on four African languages, for instance, estimated to
MIT Technology Review
that between 40% and 60% of articles in their Wikipedia editions were uncorrected machine translations. And after auditing the Wikipedia edition in Inuktitut, an Indigenous language close to Greenlandic that’s spoken in Canada,
MIT Technology Review
estimates that more than two-thirds of pages containing more than several sentences feature portions created this way.
This is beginning to cause a
wicked problem
. AI systems, from Google Translate to ChatGPT, learn to “speak” new languages by scraping huge quantities of text from the internet. Wikipedia is sometimes the largest source of online linguistic data for languages with few speakers—so any errors on those pages, grammatical or otherwise, can poison the wells that AI is expected to draw from. That can make the models’ translation of these languages particularly error-prone, which creates a sort of linguistic doom loop as people continue to add more and more poorly translated Wikipedia pages using those tools, and AI models continue to train from poorly translated pages. It’s a complicated problem, but it boils down to a simple concept:
Garbage in, garbage out
.
“These models are built on raw data,” says Kevin Scannell, a former professor of computer science at Saint Louis University who now builds computer software tailored for endangered languages. “They will try and learn everything about a language from scratch. There is no other input. There are no grammar books. There are no dictionaries. There is nothing other than the text that is inputted.”
There isn’t perfect data on the scale of this problem, particularly because a lot of AI training data is kept confidential and the field continues to evolve rapidly. But back in 2020, Wikipedia was
estimated
to make up more than half the training data that was fed into AI models translating some languages spoken by millions across Africa, including Malagasy, Yoruba, and Shona. In 2022, a research team from Germany that looked into what data could be obtained by online scraping
even found
that Wikipedia was the sole easily accessible source of online linguistic data for 27 under-resourced languages.

data.title: Microsoft in court for allegedly misleading Australians over 365 subscriptions
data.author: edwinjm
data.article_summary: 澳大利亚竞争与消费者委员会（ACCC）指控微软澳大利亚及其母公司微软公司误导约270万澳大利亚客户，在其Microsoft 365订阅计划中整合AI助手Copilot时未充分披露所有选项。ACCC称，微软自2024年10月31日起告知自动续订用户，他们要么接受含Copilot的更昂贵套餐，要么取消订阅，而隐瞒了第三种选择——价格更低且不含Copilot的"经典"套餐。该选项仅在用户开始取消订阅流程时才显示。ACCC认为此举迫使消费者接受价格涨幅达29%-45%的新套餐。ACCC已向联邦法院提起诉讼，要求处罚、禁令、赔偿消费者损失等。微软的沟通方式被指违反了澳大利亚消费者法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Microsoft强制升级订阅计划并捆绑Copilot AI功能的争议

不同观点：
• **消费者被欺骗的不满**  
  - 用户发现订阅计划被自动升级到更贵的包含Copilot版本（如美国$69→$99，家庭版$99→$129）  
  - 批评微软未明确告知是计划变更而非免费试用（jeppester、stevenkkim）  
  - 案例：89岁老人被强制升级，需投诉才退款（stevesimmons）  

• **对AI功能价值的质疑**  
  - 用户认为Copilot无用且存在幻觉（sireat），质疑AI是否值得额外付费（zerosizedweasle）  
  - 对比：Google Workspace同样因AI涨价（akulbe）  

• **应对策略与替代方案**  
  - 通过取消订阅或关闭自动续费可切换回旧版"Classic"计划（tzs、nashashmi）  
  - 部分用户选择完全取消订阅，转向Libre Office等替代品（stevenkkim、matheusmoreira）  

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：是否属于"黑暗模式"（dark patterns）故意欺骗消费者（jeppester）  
- **行业影响**：类似有线电视公司的捆绑策略（jbombadil），罚款$5000万对微软无威慑力（iptq）  
- **延伸问题**：Windows 10→11强制TPM硬件要求引发不满（loeg）  
- **用户情绪**：即使价格合理，欺骗行为导致品牌信任流失（stevenkkim、stevesimmons）

45721682.article_content:
Date
27 October 2025
Topics
Buying and selling products and services
Compliance and enforcement
The ACCC has commenced proceedings in the Federal Court against Microsoft Australia and its parent company Microsoft Corporation for allegedly misleading approximately 2.7 million Australian customers when communicating subscription options and price increases, after it integrated its AI assistant, Copilot, into Microsoft 365 plans.
The ACCC alleges that since 31 October 2024, Microsoft has told subscribers of Microsoft 365 Personal and Family plans with auto-renewal enabled that to maintain their subscription they must accept the integration of Copilot and pay higher prices for their plan, or, alternatively, cancel their subscription.
The ACCC alleges this information provided to subscribers was false or misleading because there was an undisclosed third option, the Microsoft 365 Personal or Family Classic plans, which allowed subscribers to retain the features of their existing plan, without Copilot, at the previous lower price.
Microsoft’s communication with subscribers did not refer to the existence of the “Classic” plans, and the only way subscribers could access them was to begin the process of cancelling their subscription. This involved navigating to the subscriptions section of their Microsoft account and selecting “Cancel subscription”. It was only on the following page that subscribers were given the option to instead move to the Classic plan. See a
screenshot of the cancellation page revealing the Classic plan
.
“Following a detailed investigation, we will allege in Court that Microsoft deliberately omitted reference to the Classic plans in its communications and concealed their existence until after subscribers initiated the cancellation process to increase the number of consumers on more expensive Copilot-integrated plans,” ACCC Chair Gina Cass-Gottlieb said.
“The Microsoft Office apps included in 365 subscriptions are essential in many people’s lives and given there are limited substitutes to the bundled package, cancelling the subscription is a decision many would not make lightly.”
“We’re concerned that Microsoft’s communications denied its customers the opportunity to make informed decisions about their subscription options, which included the possibility of retaining all the features of their existing plan without Copilot and at the lower price,” Ms Cass-Gottlieb said.
“We believe many Microsoft 365 customers would have opted for the Classic plan had they been aware of all the available options.”
Following the integration of Copilot, the annual subscription price of the Microsoft 365 Personal plan increased by 45 per cent from $109 to $159. The annual subscription price for the Microsoft 365 Family plan increased by 29 per cent from $139 to $179.
Microsoft sent two emails and published a blog post to inform auto-renewing subscribers (as of 31 October 2024) about the Copilot integration and the impending price increase that would apply at their next renewal. These three pieces of communication are central to the ACCC’s case.
“We allege that Microsoft’s two emails to existing subscribers and the blog post were false or misleading as they conveyed that consumers had to accept the more expensive Copilot-integrated plans, and that the only other option was to cancel,” Ms Cass-Gottlieb said.
“All businesses need to provide accurate information about their services and prices. Failure to do so risks breaching the Australian Consumer Law,” Ms Cass-Gottlieb said.
In establishing its investigation into this matter, the ACCC drew on a significant number of consumer reports, as well as commentary in online forums such as Reddit. Information provided by consumers to the ACCC’s Infocentre was critical to alerting the ACCC to the alleged conduct, particularly in identifying the availability of the Classic plan through subscribers’ cancellation flows.
The ACCC is seeking orders including penalties, injunctions, declarations, consumer redress, and costs.
Consumer response
The ACCC believes the millions of Australian consumers who were allegedly misled by Microsoft about the availability of the Classic plan may have suffered economic harm through the automatic renewal of their subscription with Copilot integration at a higher price.
The ACCC is seeking consumer redress in this case for Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscribers affected by the alleged conduct.
Existing Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscribers who have not had their subscription renewed since 8 July 2025 and would like to revert to their previous plan may be able to select the cancel option and follow the steps in the cancellation process until the Classic plan is offered. However, the ACCC notes that the subscription options and prices offered are entirely in Microsoft’s control and could be subject to change at any time.

data.title: Amazon strategised about keeping water use secret
data.author: chhum
data.article_summary: 《卫报》披露的亚马逊内部文件显示，该公司曾制定策略隐瞒其数据中心真实耗水量，2022年内部预测2030年将达77亿加仑。为避免声誉风险，亚马逊选择仅公布直接用水数据，而不计入发电等间接用水。虽然微软和谷歌定期公开用水数据，亚马逊至今未披露其服务器农场总耗水量。公司发言人辩称该文件"过时"，并强调已提高用水效率，但拒绝说明具体过时内容。批评者指出，亚马逊在干旱地区扩建数据中心的同时，其"水资源正向"计划却回避间接用水责任。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据中心的水资源使用问题及其影响

不同观点：
• **数据中心水资源使用被夸大**  
  - 认为农业用水远超过数据中心用水（[imgabe], [cm2012]）  
  - 质疑水资源是否真正被“消耗”，可能只是加热或循环利用（[avalys], [Reason077]）  
  - 数据中心的用水信息可能涉及商业机密（[londons_explore]）  

• **数据中心水资源使用存在问题**  
  - 媒体和公众讨论常带有情绪化，但双方可能都在使用误导性论据（[nzach]）  
  - 公司隐瞒用水数据，导致无法进行准确比较（[1vuio0pswjnm7]）  
  - 使用地下水可能不负责任，应优先使用地表水（[astroflection]）  

• **公司环保宣传的真实性**  
  - 质疑公司如何实现“返还比使用更多的水”（[charles_f]）  
  - 批评公司通过虚假宣传掩盖实际行为（[lpln3452]）
